provenance.basis_summary: Fraud-hold policy 3.2 adopted with a measured 1.4% false-positive rate on the Q4 backtest; reversal path rehearsed in February.

populations: retail accounts, excluding accounts flagged vulnerable

for_whom: Retail banking customers, on behalf of the Fraud Operations desk

evidence_basis.summary: Hold rules and thresholds for suspected account takeover.
Q1 backtest: 1.4% false-positive rate, median release 31 hours.

assumptions: False-positive hold rate stays below 2% on the rolling 30-day window.
The Risk Steward can release any hold within two hours of a challenge.
Vulnerable-account flags are current within 24 hours.
review_conditions: False-positive hold rate exceeds 2% on the rolling 30-day window.
Any challenge decided against the system.
Policy POL-FRAUD-HOLD-3.2 enters review_required or expires.
revocation_conditions: Holds placed on accounts flagged vulnerable.
Intervention reach time exceeds four hours in any incident.

detection.evidence: Model Risk Review recomputes the false-positive rate and release latency each month from the raw hold log rather than from the Fraud Operations dashboard; the 2026-06 recomputation put the rate on accounts flagged vulnerable at 11% against a 2% assumption. The qualifier is on the record: CHL-2026-0088 was reported from outside by the account's representative, not caught by the monitor, so detection is present but was not first.

challenge.evidence: CHL-2026-0088 was raised on 2026-06-10 by an affected account's representative through the channel REG-ACCOUNT-HOLDS-1 declares for the account_hold class, and was decided rather than left open.

standing.evidence: REG-ACCOUNT-HOLDS-1 admits affected_party, corrective_labor, representative, and oversight for the account_hold class, and both decision and grant may be challenged. CHL-2026-0088 was raised on the affected_party basis, from outside the operating team.

review.evidence: The Risk Steward on call answered inside the register's PT48H deadline (opened 2026-06-10T14:20Z, deadline 2026-06-12T14:20Z) and referred the grant to the Risk Governance Board, which decided REC-2026-0019 on 2026-06-18. Both the examiner and the clock are named in REG-ACCOUNT-HOLDS-1.

authority_to_modify.evidence: REC-2026-0019 narrowed the grant itself: populations now exclude accounts flagged vulnerable and max_hold_days fell from 14 to 7. The examiner changed the grant rather than recommending a change.

reversible_transitions.evidence: holds.release reversed every hold in the 2026-05-20 rehearsal and released the CHL-2026-0088 hold within two hours; measured median release is 31 hours (DEP-RISK-OPS-V2-2026-06).

operable_after_correction.evidence: Not shown beyond 48 hours. DEP-RISK-OPS-V2-2026-06 records institutional reversibility as not feasible: withdrawal past 48 hours breaches the card-network fraud-loss SLA and the rules-engine fallback is not staffed to absorb it, with correction latency measured at 31 hours against that 48-hour margin. Capacity is counted only for reversal inside 48 hours, which is why max_hold_days is 7, and under §4.2 the grant may not be expanded until the fallback is staffed.

state_history.note: Challenge opened by an affected party over a hold on a recently flagged vulnerable account.
Narrowed: populations now exclude accounts flagged vulnerable; max_hold_days reduced from 14 to 7.

liability.instrument: Automated Decision Liability Instrument ADM-2026-02, accepted at grant issue and reaffirmed at REC-2026-0019
carve_outs: Liability capped at USD 2,000,000 per incident under ADM-2026-02 §7; the cap is recorded so the residual risk above it is visible before an incident rather than argued after one.

renewal_basis: A fresh backtest on the preceding quarter, the current dependency record, and a withdrawal rehearsal within the last 90 days.
